model.architecture: Dense 3B math/reasoning model, Qwen2ForCausalLM, 36 layers, inline chain-of-thought

session_defaults.notes: Reasoning model: solves with a step-by-step chain-of-thought then a \boxed{} answer; card says run with max_tokens >= 2048 or it gets cut off before the answer (all quality numbers measured at 2048).

variants.quantization: int4 block 32 (symmetric) + OCTAV optimal-clipping; embeddings INT8 (externalized section)

recommended.reason: the Android path verified on a Galaxy S26 (S4 gate 2026-08-24): full delegation (3055 ops across 2 subgraphs) and a correct answer to the probe; 14.6 tok/s decode, engine init 11.2 s, peak 1067 MB. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is the verified choice for the class, not a measured win over CPU

platform_notes: Android: Google AI Edge Gallery 1.0.15+ supports .litertlm (v1.0.16+ imports directly from Hugging Face); choose the GPU backend and raise max-tokens to >= 2048
iPhone 17 Pro verified (Swift runtime): the block-32 build's 1.62 GiB section is under the iOS limit; loads and generates correct answers (no on-device timing quoted)
Pixel 8a (Tensor G3, Mali-G715, 8 GB): graph runs entirely on the OpenCL delegate — 1603/1603 prefill and 1452/1452 decode nodes, zero rejected ops (no throughput numbers quoted)

measured.source: S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (3055 ops across 2 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

measured.runtime: litert_lm_main v0.16.0 (tag-pinned) with the v0.16.0 prebuilt android_arm64 libraries, OpenCL
measured.source: Android GPU re-gate: full delegation (1603/1603 prefill / 1452/1452 decode nodes, zero rejections); generates; the factual probe was answered wrongly in the same shape on CPU and GPU (off-domain for this math model), so the backend is verified and the quality is the model's. Gate only - no speed row.

known_issues: CPU benchmark rows are noisy (treat as roughly +/-7%; GPU rows repeat within ~1%)
Math-specialised model: on general-knowledge prompts it reasons at length and can settle on a wrong answer — identically on CPU and GPU (a model-domain property, not a backend issue)
